Native dependencies
===================

deps/build.sh (Linux, macOS) and deps/build.ps1 (Windows, from a Visual Studio
developer prompt) fetch and build everything below. The engine
needs these four directories, given to cargo as environment variables:

  BORINGSSL_DIR  BoringSSL 148a7b1f (2026-11-13) + patches/boringssl.patch
  NGHTTP2_DIR    nghttp2 v1.71.0 + patches/nghttp2.patch
  LIBUV_DIR      libuv v1.53.0, unmodified
  CPPCORO_DIR    cppcoro from andreasbuhr/cppcoro 8642e985 (C++20 coroutines)

Each is a source tree with its CMake build in a build/ subdirectory. The crate
also expects cxx-async 1575822a + patches/cxx-async.patch in deps/cxx-async.

Without the variables only the Rust side compiles, which is enough for clippy.

The patches
-----------

boringssl.patch
  SSL_set_write_cipher_list_override, SSL_set_write_supported_versions_override:
  write these ClientHello lists exactly as given (stock BoringSSL fixes their
  contents and order). SSL_set_signature_algorithm_grease: turn the GREASE value
  in signature_algorithms off while keeping GREASE elsewhere (Safari).
  SSL_set_client_hello_padding: RFC 7685 padding to 512 bytes, which BoringSSL
  dropped (Safari still pads). Verify preferences may repeat a value (Safari
  lists rsa_pss_rsae_sha384 twice).

nghttp2.patch
  RFC 7540 priorities in HEADERS and nghttp2_submit_priority work again (upstream
  ignores them since RFC 9113; Chrome still sends them). Per-field HPACK flags:
  NGHTTP2_NV_FLAG_INDEX, NGHTTP2_NV_FLAG_WITHOUT_INDEXING,
  NGHTTP2_NV_FLAG_HUFFMAN, NGHTTP2_NV_FLAG_NO_HUFFMAN, so the encoder can follow
  a browser's choices instead of nghttp2's heuristic.

cxx-async.patch
  The C++ side returned the new channel by value while the Rust side writes it
  through an out pointer given as the first argument. That only lines up where
  the hidden return pointer is the first argument (x86-64); on arm64 it goes in
  x8, so every coroutine crashed on Apple Silicon. The channel is now built in
  place through an explicit pointer. Also: GCC rejects the leading "::" in the
  coroutine_traits specialization, and MSVC needs /std:c++20 for cxx-async's
  own source.

Windows
-------

deps/build.ps1 does the same with Ninja and MSVC. BoringSSL is built without
assembly (OPENSSL_NO_ASM) so no NASM is needed. Dot-source it so the variables
stay set:

  . deps/build.ps1
